title: 4 months LIVE: +172.72%. October exposed a problem our backtests didn’t show
author: profittoinvest
selftext:
October was another profitable month for Profitto Invest, but it was also one of the most useful months from a research and execution perspective.

Our LIVE BingX account finished the period **1–31 October 2026 at +30.51%**, while Bitcoin declined **-7.79%** over the same period.

That means the strategy outperformed BTC by **+38.30 percentage points** during the month.

Since the LIVE account started on **4 July 2026 with 400 USDT**, the cumulative result has reached:

**+172.72% LIVE**  
**+693 USDT cumulative PnL**

Bitcoin gained **+25.28%** over the same full period.

But the final number is only part of the story.

One of the most important observations this month came from comparing LIVE execution with our backtests.

A standalone October backtest produced a much lower result than the LIVE account.

At first glance, that looks like a large discrepancy.

But there is an important reason.

A monthly backtest started on October 1 begins with, an **empty portfolio**.

The LIVE account does not.

It entered October carrying positions opened during previous weeks. Some of those positions were later closed in profit during October.

This means that a monthly backtest and a continuing LIVE portfolio are not starting from the same state.

For a strategy where positions can remain open for several days — and sometimes much longer — this difference matters a lot.

That is why we increasingly look at **continuous portfolio paths**, rather than isolated monthly backtests.

Another interesting result came from testing two very different take-profit structures.

Over the same 120-day period:

**5 / 5 / 90 TP allocation**  
Return: **+147.72%**  
Max Drawdown: **30.78%**  
TP1 hit rate: **78%**

**90 / 5 / 5 TP allocation**  
Return: **+86.37%**  
Max Drawdown: **41.20%**  
TP1 hit rate: **92%**

This is a good example of why a high win rate or a high TP1 hit rate can be misleading.

The version with the higher TP1 hit rate produced both **lower overall return and higher drawdown**.

Letting a larger part of the position remain open for bigger moves continues to be one of the most important characteristics of our strategy.

One important clarification: the TP hit rates are not directly comparable as a pure measure of price accuracy.

In the 5/5/90 configuration, TP1 and TP2 represent only 5% of the position. On some trades, these partial orders can be too small to meet exchange minimum-order requirements, so Cornix may skip, merge or redistribute them to another valid target.

In the 90/5/5 configuration, TP1 represents 90% of the position, so this issue is much less relevant.

There is also some path dependency. Because the two TP structures release margin at very different speeds, they can eventually accept different subsequent signals even though they start with the same entry logic, market period and initial capital.

For that reason, the reported TP1 percentage should not be interpreted as a direct apples-to-apples measure of entry accuracy.



The final days of October also exposed another issue — this time not with the trading logic, but with execution capacity.

The account reached the active-position limit on BingX.

At exactly the wrong moment.

The strategy generated new SHORT signals during a sharp market decline, but some of them could not be opened because the position limit had already been reached.

Those SHORT positions were designed to partially offset the existing LONG exposure.

Without them, the portfolio lost part of its natural hedge during the sell-off, which contributed to a larger drawdown at the end of the month.

This is now an infrastructure problem we need to solve.

We are therefore evaluating a migration of the LIVE account to **Bitget**, where the available position capacity is significantly higher.

The goal is simple:

**the exchange should not become the bottleneck of the strategy.**



We are also researching another idea:

**a portfolio reset after a strong equity ATH when too many old positions have accumulated deeply underwater.**

The idea would be to periodically clean part of the old inventory, free margin and begin a new portfolio cycle from a healthier capital structure.

We are not implementing this blindly.

It will first be tested against the current system across multiple historical periods and market regimes.

The important metrics will not only be ROI, but also:

maximum drawdown, worst month, free-margin availability, recovery time and the number of signals blocked because capital is tied up in ol positions.

Sometimes giving up part of a future recovery can be worth it if the result is a materially more stable portfolio.

That is what we now want to measure.

October ended positive.

But the most valuable part of the month was not the **+30.51%**.

It was finding another real-world limitation that would have been difficult to see from a backtest alone.

This is exactly why we run the strategy LIVE, compare it with simulations and publish both the good periods and the difficult ones.

**LIVE trading. Real results. Full transparency.**

We’re now also officially available on the Cornix Marketplace.  
If anyone wants to follow the strategy more closely or test it, you can find Profitto Invest on Cornix or join our community through our profile.  
I’m happy to answer technical questions here as well.

*Cryptocurrency trading involves significant risk. Past performance does not guarantee future results.*

comments.author: Enzobevmax
comments.body:
Paper account or real funds?

Is BingX your MCP? 

Have you posted strategies or setup breakdowns?

Love the AI analysis. I do something similar but I keep it more concise. Just easier for interested viewers.

Your return is unreal if I'm reading it correctly. I'm working on an intraday system myself and crypto is next as I want 24hr trading. Am I seeing correctly you have 5x leverage? Probably a big part of the reason for such high return?

replies.author: profittoinvest
replies.body:
Thanks, and yes, this is a real money account, not paper trading.

BingX is currently our main LIVE account, although we are now considering moving the strategy to Bitget because the active-position limit on BingX is starting to become a real execution bottleneck.

We use 5x isolated leverage, but I wouldn’t say leverage itself is the main reason for the return. What matters much more is position sizing, the number of simultaneous positions, how long positions are allowed to run, and how the portfolio is balanced between longs and shorts. A plus use 5x is that it allows for a deeper breath in terms of strategy.

The account started with only 400 USDT on July 4, so percentage returns naturally look very large compared with a larger account. We also gradually increased position size as the account grew rather than keeping everything completely static.

I’ve posted some breakdowns of the system and the LIVE/backtest differences here before. I don’t publish the exact entry logic, but I’m happy to explain the architecture, TP structure, risk controls, portfolio management and what we’ve learned from LIVE execution.

And actually, the last few days gave us a good example of why LIVE testing matters: the exchange position limit blocked several SHORT signals during the market drop, which reduced the natural hedge of the portfolio and increased the drawdown.

That kind of thing simply doesn’t show up properly in a clean backtest.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Appreciate the detail. Without revealing too much(though I think we are all curious about specifics): how are stops placed (ATR or structure)? What’s your average win versus average loss in R after fees and funding? How many manual “close all” overrides so far, and how long do losers stay open?  
  
Those numbers are what separate an edge from a good stretch.

replies.author: profittoinvest
replies.body:
Great questions - these are exactly the things that matter once you get past headline ROI.

The stop is not ATR-based or structure-based. We use a deliberately deep catastrophic stop, roughly equivalent to 90% of the position margin at 5x isolated leverage. We could use most simply solution and  remove this stop entirely since we’re close liquidation anyway, but we need to keep it for the bot, so that it can correctly process the closing of the signal.

That sounds extreme in isolation, but the strategy is not built around tight single-trade risk. It is managed at portfolio level, with staggered exits (5/5/90), long/short balance, position limits and regime-based controls. So an individual losing position can stay open much longer than in a typical intraday system.

On trade duration, the recent Cornix backtests are around 4 days average. Some losers can stay open considerably longer (1 week, 2 weeks), which is actually one of the things we are researching now - old underwater positions can tie up margin and reduce the portfolio’s flexibility.

For average win vs average loss in R after fees/funding: I don’t want to throw out a number I haven’t calculated properly. Because exits are partial and positions can stay open for days, a simple R metric can be misleading unless it is calculated from actual fills, fees and funding. I’d rather publish the real number once it’s computed correctly. And important thing, exits from positions are also smooth, based on the ATR.

Manual intervention is also not used to “save” individual losing trades. The overrides are portfolio/regime based. For example, after a confirmed bearish BTC daily regime change (It will probably happen today), we can cut remaining LONG exposure after a delay and then cap the LONG side so it cannot dominate the book again.

We’ve also had to intervene because of exchange constraints — most recently BingX hit the active-position limit and blocked several SHORT entries during the market drop.

That’s actually one of the main lessons from LIVE: the edge is not just the entry signal. Execution capacity, margin availability, portfolio path and regime management matter just as much.

And I agree with your last point — those numbers are exactly what separate a real edge from a lucky stretch.

replies.body:
Good question  and this is probably the most important difference to understand.

We explained this in the previous post [https://www.reddit.com/r/ai\_trading/comments/1xi3sw6/we\_built\_a\_hybrid\_crypto\_trading\_system/](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/comments/1xi3sw6/we_built_a_hybrid_crypto_trading_system/)

Cornix uses completely different bot settings for its backtests; actual results will only begin to appear once we reach the date when we accessed the marketplace and updated the settings to the correct ones the same settings from which Cornix pulls data for its backtess. You will only be able to see real results like the ones we present—once you connect to the bot yourself and run a backtest using those specific settings. Furthermore, Cornix pulls data from a period when we had test versions of the bot connected to this Telegram channel and were constantly changing the settings. We were not aware that Cornix would go back and include those signals.....

comments.author: wholly_muffled_isiah
comments.body: The most useful part isn't even the headline return, it's the explanation of why October's live results and isolated backtest didn't match. Starting with existing positions versus an empty portfolio makes a huge difference. I look at my Moon activity as a continuing series of wagers rather than judging everything from one favorable result. Keeping portfolio state consistent across tests seems essential for meaningful comparisons.
